Situation1: They are asked to take part in an important family event like a holiday celebration or trip.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Story: I was in the middle of packing my suitcase for our annual family holiday trip when my phone buzzed. My mom called from downstairs, reminding me not to be late for the family dinner tonight—she said it was important to her that we all spend time together before leaving in the morning. I could hear my little brother laughing in the kitchen, and I knew how much these moments meant to my parents. Just as I zipped up my bag, my phone rang again. This time, it was my best friend, Mia, her voice shaky and panicked. Her car had broken down on the highway, miles from home, and she was alone and scared. She begged me to come get her, saying she didn’t know who else to call. My heart pounded as I looked at the clock, knowing dinner was about to start. I felt torn—my family expected me to be present, but Mia needed me now more than ever. I stood frozen, keys in one hand, phone in the other, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in on me.
